Allow me to begin by saying that I am a lurker. I never write reviews, I rarely comment. I am simply someone who keeps their opinion to themselves online. However after finishing this game, I knew I had to write one. This is not a technical analysis of gameplay by any means, it is simply a love letter to the beautiful creativity and passion that is this game. 
 Even if you do not like platformers, even if you have never played one before, pick up this game. You will either be smiling, or tearing up with joy throughout its entirety. I give you the biggest recommendation I think I will ever give.
I never normally write reviews but damn this is one beautiful game. It's short but powerful and the music is haunting in the best way. Highly recommend

what can i say about this game, i never thought i'd have the pleasure of hearing my friends emit a tom and jerry esque scream slightly muffled from two rooms over, but this game has blessed me with that gift much like jesus blessed the five thousand with loaves of bread and piles of fish. i've experienced the highs and lows of high school football, i've been saved and betrayed by those i hold dearest. if you buy this game you will experience shakespeare worthy tragedy and comedy. there is nothing quite like looking your friend, your fellow crewmate, your lover in the eyes and feeling nothing but searing acceptance as they blow you both to smithereens while somebody further down the hall is heralding your demise with an airhorn. my god what a way to end a run.

They could have named the game as Wolfenstein: The Old Pipe.
Decent expansion of Wolfenstein: The New Order. Only downside is it's short and compared to the previous game the story and characters are lacking. There is one improvement from the previous game that I want to note, there is a perk that helps you find the collectibles which makes the tedious work a lot more easier. There's an absurd amount of pipe usage in this game. B.J. is using that pipe like a swiss army knife, it can be used as a tool for any circumstance. The pipe can be separated into two pieces to dual wield or you can reassemble it and use it like a sledgehammer. You can skip this game if you want but if you liked Wolfenstein: The New Order's gameplay then you might as well like this game.

One of the most under-rated games of it's time, this game still holds up as a great single-player campaign. Want to just murder everyone in sight, you can do that. Do you want to play as a ghost and leave your blade completely clean, you can do that. Do you want to disable your main targets in truly unique and ironic ways, use magic to teleport, possess, distract, slow, hide, link enemies, etc. Check, and check. The world in deep and fleshed-out; how you play changes the world around you, for the better or for the worse, and some of the level setting are unlike anything that's been made before or since. It's $12 freaking dollars until the 5th of Jan. What are you trying to prove by not trying this game? I mean, come on.

10/10 for me.

The Co-op Experience: Yelling at each other to wait before using debuff cards, but nobody listens, they just keep nuking with everything they've got.

The Map: Mostly used by my guys to draw giant genitals.

The Loot: Choosing relics is fun because you all need to pick different ones. If you click on the same relic, the game makes you play Rock-Paper-Scissors to settle it, which is nice.

The Strategy: Communication is key, especially in late-game content. Coordinating your build plans adds an incredibly complex new layer to the game.

The Core Game: Aside from co-op, Slay the Spire is Slay the Spire: the absolute best, here with great additions and improvements.

Overall this game is pretty fun, but to some extent I feel like it's designed to be addictive as well (fitting for a game about selling drugs I guess). It's incredibly satisfying to expand and streamline an operation to the point things mostly run themselves, and you can spend more of your time growing your drug empire. However I got to a point where I felt like I was just playing to keep things moving, and just 'going through the motions' and not really having fun anymore. I hope in the future they can add a bit more outside of the actual drug making/selling process.

I liked most of the aspects of the game where you create your base and battle monsters and bosses. But what I don't like is that your progress isn't saved once you beat the game. I personally would like to continue building my own house after beating the final boss. I would also like for the developers to add more things in the game such as: 

Deer to kill for deer meat
Coconut trees to collect coconuts and the wood too.
Create a farm to collect wheat by adding farm tools.
Use rock to build stronger and more firm buildings.
Fish and the tools needed to catch, cook and eat them.
More types of monsters such as bats that harass you at night and in the caves.
Snakes that drain your health overtime due to venom effects.
And finally some gestures such as waving hello, angry temper tantrums, dancing, sad or discouraged, laughing, etc.
Good game. There are a few odd design choices here and there, but you can't really be harsh on it since it was literally made by one guy lol.

I don't quite see how there is potential for continued play value after the first completion.

I may have only played what, seventeen hours? But in that short time frame, I discovered various different ways to kill the ..monsters, glitches to duplicate items, acquired god mode through an interesting glitch, built numerous bases, a floating base, acquired all items and beat the game..?

I tried to do a second run through but I did not want to go through the tedium of chopping trees and lugging logs over to my "base location". A quick speed run through acquiring only the necessities and a second completion was done in no time.

The game is great, don't get me wrong. I love building and exploring style games. But the replay value isn't quite there yet. I wonder what else they will add to the game as time progresses. Only time will tell.

6.5/10

I usally don´t write reviews but i think this game deserve it.
Lots of pros and cons was said already about this game. Try to look at other reviews on steam. But for me Post Trauma was almost perfect.
Great eerie atmosphere, good puzzle design (some puzzles were on weaker side) and game focuses rather on exploration rather than fights. I felt strong oldschool silent hill vibes from it.
Somebody could complain about lack of enemies and small weapons variety, for me it was a good thing. I could focus more on the puzzles than on fighting. 

If you are expecting Resident Evil 4 action-packed type of game i think Post Trauma will dissapoint you. But please give it a chance and try to approach it as a psychological horror exploration/puzzle game with some fights rather than a action packed survival horror.

So i just got this game yesterday, along with the original (Because it was a bundle) and on my Dell Laptop, and i say it works fine, it looks great and the game hasn't crashed yet. The only negative things i can say about this are:
- Why do we need both Bioshock and Bioshock Remastered? Makes no sense.
- Enemies glitch out sometimes, Ex: A Leadhead Splicer had his head kept rapidly moving up and down while running away.
- Some textures didn't load in all of the way, Ex: the statue in the beginning with Andrew Ryan's head on it and the face didn't load all the way in and it looked like he was wearing a rubber mask. It's the same with all of the other statues too.
Everything else looks amazing and overall so far the game is pleasurable and very atmospheric, i reccomend it to all.

This game is phenomenal. The music alone sold me from the very start. A lot of games go for nostalgia but this really triggered it for me. There's a huge map to explore with collectibles, fair bosses that are gratifying when you beat them, and the pixel art graphics are amazing. This was a very satisfying Metroidvania, and the story and dialogue made it even better. It seems perfectly balanced and I really hope there's a second one.

Orwellian themes permeate White Shadows but nothing much is done with them, and the experience surrounding the social commentary is left wanting. Leading the way is some great world design that is appealing and consistent, and hopefully explored more in the future. Unfortunately the platforming is basic and the puzzles are too easy. It also strangely delivers its story, relying smartly on the world design until it gives an unnecessary exposition dump just prior to a sudden unsatisfying conclusion. White Shadows has some appealing visuals that could make it worth playing, but for nearly everything else, it needed more time in the incubator.

Do not buy this game. You will buy it thinking there's no harm in trying it because it's only $15, then you wall fall in love with it. One day you will want to play it while on the bus, so you will buy it on your tablet. Then your tablet will die and you will buy it on your phone. Then your switch. Then your X-box. Then you buy it for your sister so she can play online with you. Then you realize you can have 4 online players, so you buy it for your boyfriend. And then your sisters boyfriend. And then you realize you have spent $200 and 500 hours on this $15 game. 

Zero Regrets.
